- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk premium or reversal bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; dampen forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for lagged sentiment influence and adjust forecast mid-period.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply downward bias of 1–2% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for suppressed sentiment effect.
- When sentiment is high and price is near recent high, model often overestimates; apply mean reversion correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast if price > 1.5% above recent peak.
